land.text: the island of Jamaica: 'The island belonged to Spain under the name Santiago until 1655' and was then English, Spain recognising English possession 'with the Treaty of Madrid (1670)'

predecessors.note: The dossier colony-of-jamaica (1655 to 6 August 1962) was written in parallel and ends with the independence. Cliopatria has no colonial Jamaica row: its British Colonial Empire shape holds Jamaica (51 cells) to 1962.

correction.text: the island of Jamaica as it stands in Cliopatria's shape from 1963, held from independence on 6 August 1962: 'Jamaica achieved independence from the United Kingdom on 6 August 1962.'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Jamaica begins in 1963 but independence was on 6 August 1962 (infobox 'Granted: 6 August 1962'). Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shape still holds all of Jamaica in 1962, so the island is drawn as British land for 1962 unless this keyframe is used; the shape itself is unchanged.

13,346 km2 against the infobox 10,991 km2 (ratio 1.21): inside a factor of two, the shape is a coastal outline slightly wider than the land. Its bbox (17.71 to 18.54 N, 78.39 to 76.12 W) is the main island; the Morant and Pedro Cays, which the page puts 'some 50-80 km off the south coast', and the Cayman Islands (a separate British territory, 215 km away on the page) are outside it. Verified for 1963 to 2023; the page records no territorial change after independence.
Identical to the 1963 shape; the page records no territorial change to 2024.

region.text: the island of Jamaica, independent of the United Kingdom

ledger.note: 6 August 1962: Jamaica becomes independent. 'Jamaica achieved independence from the United Kingdom on 6 August 1962.' 'The new state retained, however, its membership in the Commonwealth of Nations.' Second page (West Indies Federation): Jamaica left the Federation after a September 1961 referendum (54 percent for leaving) and the Federation was dissolved on 31 May 1962. The matching loss is the dissolve event of colony-of-jamaica; Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shape still holds Jamaica in 1962 and drops it only in 1963.

certainty.note: An island state: the coast is the frontier and the pages record no land boundary or later territorial change. The offshore cays (Morant, Pedro) are named on the page without dates or limits; they are not in Cliopatria's shape.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2 (Jamaica, West Indies Federation). Cliopatria's Jamaica starts in 1963, one year after independence (6 August 1962); the new keyframe jamaica_1962 fills the year. The colonial predecessor colony-of-jamaica and the west-indies-federation (3 January 1958 to 31 May 1962) already have dossiers (written in parallel, not read by me beyond their identity and ledger), so Jamaica's found event names colony-of-jamaica as counterpart. Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shape holds Jamaica's 51 cells to 1962 and none from 1963, so the british-colonial-empire dossier (eu-11) should carry the matching loss in August 1962. The Jamaica page gives no year for the Federation referendum (the West Indies Federation page says September 1961). Pages do not date any Jamaican territorial claim (Pedro Bank, Navassa): the page is silent. Disagreement not settled here: the Federation page has the Cayman Islands and Turks and Caicos, 'attached to Jamaica' within the Federation, separating from Jamaica in 1962, while the colony-of-jamaica dossier (reading the Colony of Jamaica infobox, a page I did not open) dates their detachment to 4 July 1959. They are in neither Cliopatria's Jamaica shape nor this dossier. No rulers listed (a Commonwealth realm; the page names only the present king). Reviewer am-08-j (2026-10-19): west-indies-federation moved out of predecessors, which list the states whose land this state took at its birth: the Federation was disestablished on 31 May 1962 (West Indies Federation infobox) and its own dossier hands Jamaica to colony-of-jamaica, from which Jamaica took the island on 6 August 1962. Jamaica was a Federation province from 1958 ('In 1958 it became a province in the Federation of the West Indies', Jamaica page) and voted to leave in September 1961 (54 percent, Federation page).
